summary: Rabbi Soffer explores the Mishnaic laws regarding the grouping of animals for Maaser Behemah, specifically focusing on the distance animals can graze and the role of the shepherd as a counter. He further examines the status of the Yarden as a boundary that separates groups of animals and discusses the sources of the Yarden and the Prat rivers in relation to halakhic concerns about water purity and mikvaot.
questions: How far apart can animals be to be considered a single group for Maaser Behemah?
Does the Yarden river act as a boundary that prevents animals from being grouped together?
Is the Yarden river considered a boundary along its entire length?
What is the source of the Yarden and Prat rivers?
Why would one be concerned about using a flowing river as a mikveh?
